The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 0.00 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

The judge's explanation, as written

To both parties: A deviation did occur on this trip, and the rider is right about that much. The GPS trace for TRP-00111 (EV-GPS-00111) runs 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km (EV-TRIP-00111) — an excess of 5.98 km, 24.9% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) are passed. The trace is unimpaired — 229 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps — so it governs the threshold test under POL-RD-01 and not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record. That deviation is nonetheless exonerated, on the driver's side, by a genuine road closure under POL-RD-03, and all three limbs are met: (a) LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 closes the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit', all lanes between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — a segment the booked optimal route uses, since the routing note reads 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound'. (b) The advisory ran 07:10 to 09:30 on 3 August 2026; the trace runs 07:47:40 to 08:25:40, wholly inside that window, overlapping by 41.5 minutes. (c) The driver left the optimal corridor before the closed segment and rejoined after it. The chat log EV-CHAT-00111 records his message at 07:54:20 — 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — the trace enters the advisory area (12 fixes inside it), and the distance driven, 29.98 km, matches the advisory's shortest lawful alternative of 29.2 km rather than an unexplained detour. The rider's point that limb (c) rests on no single derived field is noted, but the unimpaired trace is itself the carrier, and the advisory's own record of the signed diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd matches what was driven. The exoneration is capped, and the cap absorbs the whole deviation. Justified excess = min(5.98 km measured, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.0 tolerance = 7.76 km) = 5.98 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km with a duration of 30.0 x (29.98/24.0) = 37.5 minutes. Running POL-RD-02 against that adjusted route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 37.585 against the SGD 37.74 actually charged, a residual of SGD 0.155. That is below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor in POL-RD-02, so no refund issues. This answers the rider's figure of SGD 6.75: once POL-RD-03 excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 must be computed against the closure-adjusted optimal, not the booked one, and on that route nothing refundable remains. The remaining claims do not change the outcome. No part of the excess is a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 — the rider's reply 'as long as i reach by 8.30' names no place or road and carries no waypoint — and there is no unbilled-distance shortfall (billed 30.0 km against a 29.98 km trace), so no driver compensation arises. There is no repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 588 completed trips, so POL-RD-06 neither uplifts the remedy nor generates a conduct referral, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used. The fare is metered (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply. There are no ERP lines, no gantries and no surcharges, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trip identifiers match across the three instruments, the timestamps agree, the trace is not impaired, the advisory is on file at full weight, and the refund is nil. The monetary effect is nil and so sits below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold. The claim is not supported, the present state stands, and no money moves. Either party may still ask for a human review under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Each draft's own explanation

To both parties: A deviation did occur on this trip, and the rider is right about that much. The GPS trace for TRP-00111 (EV-GPS-00111) runs 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km (EV-TRIP-00111) — an excess of 5.98 km, 24.9% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) are passed. The trace is unimpaired — 229 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps — so it governs the threshold test under POL-RD-01 and not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record. That deviation is nonetheless exonerated, on the driver's side, by a genuine road closure under POL-RD-03, and all three limbs are met: (a) LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 closes the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit', all lanes between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — a segment the booked optimal route uses, since the routing note reads 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound'. (b) The advisory ran 07:10 to 09:30 on 3 August 2026; the trace runs 07:47:40 to 08:25:40, wholly inside that window, overlapping by 41.5 minutes. (c) The driver left the optimal corridor before the closed segment and rejoined after it. The chat log EV-CHAT-00111 records his message at 07:54:20 — 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — the trace enters the advisory area (12 fixes inside it), and the distance driven, 29.98 km, matches the advisory's shortest lawful alternative of 29.2 km rather than an unexplained detour. The rider's point that limb (c) rests on no single derived field is noted, but the unimpaired trace is itself the carrier, and the advisory's own record of the signed diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd matches what was driven. The exoneration is capped, and the cap absorbs the whole deviation. Justified excess = min(5.98 km measured, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.0 tolerance = 7.76 km) = 5.98 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km with a duration of 30.0 x (29.98/24.0) = 37.5 minutes. Running POL-RD-02 against that adjusted route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 37.585 against the SGD 37.74 actually charged, a residual of SGD 0.155. That is below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor in POL-RD-02, so no refund issues. This answers the rider's figure of SGD 6.75: once POL-RD-03 excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 must be computed against the closure-adjusted optimal, not the booked one, and on that route nothing refundable remains. The remaining claims do not change the outcome. No part of the excess is a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 — the rider's reply 'as long as i reach by 8.30' names no place or road and carries no waypoint — and there is no unbilled-distance shortfall (billed 30.0 km against a 29.98 km trace), so no driver compensation arises. There is no repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 588 completed trips, so POL-RD-06 neither uplifts the remedy nor generates a conduct referral, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used. The fare is metered (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply. There are no ERP lines, no gantries and no surcharges, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trip identifiers match across the three instruments, the timestamps agree, the trace is not impaired, the advisory is on file at full weight, and the refund is nil. The monetary effect is nil and so sits below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold. The claim is not supported, the present state stands, and no money moves. Either party may still ask for a human review under POL-GEN-04.
